chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out on the Day of Sacrifice to the rear of the city upon a camel that was bare-backed (without a saddle). So he passed by the women, stopped by them, and then said: 'O group of women! Give charity and obey your husbands, for most of you will be in the Fire.'

When they heard that, they wept. Then a woman from among them stood up to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! In the Fire along with the disbelievers? By Allah, we are not disbelievers, so we should become from the inhabitants of the Fire.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'You are disbelievers by virtue of the rights of your husbands.'

key_terms.كَافِرَاتٌ بِحَقِّ أَزْوَاجِكُنَّ: Disbelievers by virtue of the rights of your husbands
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet mean when he tells women they are 'disbelievers' in relation to their husbands?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the theological weight of marital obedience by linking women's spiritual fate to their conduct toward husbands, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding 'nushuz' (disobedience). The Prophet’s clarification that 'kufr' here denotes 'kufr al-a'mal' (disbelief of action) rather than 'kufr al-i'tiqad' (disbelief of creed) prevents misunderstanding of their eternal status, while the setting on Eid al-Adhar underscores the communal obligation of charity alongside domestic duties.
